rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The chemical industry is the economy's upstream multiplier: raw materials in, value-added products out, and every sector — agriculture, textiles, construction, health — downstream of at least one process. Heavy chemicals compete per tonne in continuous plants; fine chemicals compete per gram in batch plants — economics, not chemistry, assigns the class.…

rows.text: **NEB-style (5m): Define the chemical industry and distinguish heavy chemicals from fine chemicals, giving two examples of each.** — **Definition:** the industry that converts raw materials (minerals, crude oil, air, water, biomass) into useful products by large-scale chemical transformation, adding value at each step.…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): "The chemical industry is the economy's multiplier, not its showcase." Explain this statement with two worked examples.** — **Meaning:** chemical products are rarely the consumer's final purchase, yet they enter the supply chain of nearly every final good — the industry's importance is upstream and multiplied.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Distinguish heavy vs fine chemicals by volume AND value - quoting only one axis loses the mark.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Value is created at each transformation step - the industry's function is the value ladder, not the molecule.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Chemical industry: large-scale conversion of raw materials into higher-value products. Classes: heavy (bulk, cheap: H2SO4, NH3, NaOH), fine/specialty (small volume, high value: pharma, dyes), consumer (soaps, fertilisers).…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Every modern sector - food, clothing, shelter, health - sits downstream of at least one chemical process.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Chemical Industry: What It Is and Why It Matters The chemical industry converts raw materials — minerals, crude oil, biomass, air, water — into useful products by chemical transformation.…  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror - **Definition:** the industry whose primary activity is the large-scale chemical conversion of raw materials into products with higher value. - **Classification by scale and value:** heavy chemicals (bulk, cheap, tonnage — sulphuric acid, ammonia, caustic soda); fine/specialty chemicals (small volume, high value — pharmaceuticals, dyes, reagents);…  ·  ## 3. Deep Conceptual — Value Is Created at Each Transformation Step - Raw ore is worth little; the metal extracted from it is worth more; the alloy shaped from the metal more still. The chemical industry's economic function is precisely this ladder: each step consumes energy, knowledge, and capital, and each step adds value disproportionate to its mass.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Mitosis produces genetically different cells. ✅ Mitosis produces genetically identical diploid daughter cells.  ·  ❌ Meiosis produces identical cells. ✅ Meiosis produces 4 genetically diverse haploid gametes.  ·  ❌ Crossing over occurs in mitosis. ✅ Crossing over occurs in Prophase I of meiosis only.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ All enzymes are proteins. ✅ Most enzymes are proteins; some RNA molecules (ribozymes) also have catalytic activity.  ·  ❌ ATP is the only energy currency. ✅ GTP, UTP, and CTP also serve as energy carriers in specific pathways.  ·  ❌ Photosynthesis occurs in all plant cells. ✅ Photosynthesis occurs only in cells containing chloroplasts (mainly mesophyll).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Respiration and photosynthesis are opposite processes with same equation. ✅ They are complementary but occur in different organelles and under different conditions.  ·  ❌ Oxygen is produced during respiration. ✅ Oxygen is consumed in aerobic respiration; produced during photosynthesis.  ·  ❌ Food chain shows all feeding relationships. ✅ Food chain is linear; food web shows interconnected feeding relationships.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ 90% of energy is transferred to next trophic level. ✅ Only ~10% energy transfers; ~90% lost as heat.  ·  ❌ Biomagnification decreases toxin concentration up the food chain. ✅ Biomagnification increases toxin concentration at higher trophic levels.  ·  ❌ Carbon cycle only involves plants and animals. ✅ Carbon cycle involves atmosphere, oceans, fossils, rocks, and decomposers.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Nitrogen fixation only occurs in bacteria. ✅ Some lightning and industrial processes (Haber) also fix nitrogen.  ·  ❌ All fungi are harmful. ✅ Many fungi are beneficial (decomposers, mycorrhizae, food, antibiotics like penicillin).  ·  ❌ Viruses are living organisms. ✅ Viruses are acellular — they cannot reproduce without a host and lack metabolism.
